X1.name: Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition for small-scale landscaping (e.g., 'The Deere Lawn Tractor: One tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.') Group B receives a small-farm focused proposition for versatile agricultural and garden tasks (e.g., 'The Deere Lawn Tractor: A single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping, built for durability and reliability.') Both groups see the same product description and price point.
X1.sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners with small gardens and 250 small-farm owners. Recruited via online panels to ensure geographic diversity.
X1.measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and willingness to pay a premium (percentage willing to pay at least 10% more than the base price).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group A.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), conclude T1 is more likely. If Group B's average purchase intent is at least 1.5 points higher and the difference is statistically significant, conclude T2 is more likely. If neither difference meets the threshold, the test is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging Deere’s tractor engineering to offer a single, integrated tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping. This aligns with the 1962 lawn equipment sales surge and the existing consumer market entry, and it provides a clear use case for homeowners.
final.target_customer: Individual homeowners with small gardens who need a single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.
final.value_proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and reliability of a tractor with the convenience of a single tool, reducing the need for multiple devices and saving time and effort.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay for the differentiated proposition.
final.uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated lawn tractor is uncertain. The test will clarify whether purchase intent and willingness to pay are driven by consumer or small-farm messaging.
would_change_if: If the test shows that small-farm owners express higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than homeowners, the recommendation would shift to a small-farm focused proposition.
If neither group meets the purchase intent threshold, the recommendation would remain to maintain the current B2B2C model without expansion.

arguments.name: Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition for small-scale landscaping (e.g., 'The Deere Lawn Tractor: One tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.') Group B receives a small-farm focused proposition for versatile agricultural and garden tasks (e.g., 'The Deere Lawn Tractor: A single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping, built for durability and reliability.') Both groups see the same product description and price point.
arguments.sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners with small gardens and 250 small-farm owners. Recruited via online panels to ensure geographic diversity.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and willingness to pay a premium (percentage willing to pay at least 10% more than the base price).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group A.

arguments.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), conclude T1 is more likely. If Group B's average purchase intent is at least 1.5 points higher and the difference is statistically significant, conclude T2 is more likely. If neither difference meets the threshold, the test is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

arguments.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging Deere’s tractor engineering to offer a single, integrated tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping. This aligns with the 1962 lawn equipment sales surge and the existing consumer market entry, and it provides a clear use case for homeowners.

Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging Deere’s tractor engineering to offer a single, integrated tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping. This aligns with the 1962 lawn equipment sales surge and the existing consumer market entry, and it provides a clear use case for homeowners.
arguments.target_customer: Individual homeowners with small gardens who need a single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.
arguments.value_proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and reliability of a tractor with the convenience of a single tool, reducing the need for multiple devices and saving time and effort.
arguments.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay for the differentiated proposition.
arguments.uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated lawn tractor is uncertain. The test will clarify whether purchase intent and willingness to pay are driven by consumer or small-farm messaging.
would_change_if: If the test shows that small-farm owners express higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than homeowners, the recommendation would shift to a small-farm focused proposition.
If neither group meets the purchase intent threshold, the recommendation would remain to maintain the current B2B2C model without expansion.

X1.name: Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition emphasizing convenience, single-tool functionality, and homeowner benefits; Group B receives a small-farm-focused proposition emphasizing versatility, multiple task capability, and small-farm owner benefits. Both groups are shown a product description of a differentiated lawn tractor (e.g., Deere 4010) and asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).
X1.sample: 300 participants: 150 homeowners (small‑scale gardens) and 150 small‑farm owners (hobby farmers). Recruited via an online panel to match demographic distribution of target markets.
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each group.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 2 points higher than Group B, proceed with developing a differentiated consumer proposition (supports T1). If Group B’s score is at least 2 points higher, proceed with a small‑farm focused proposition (supports T2). If the difference is less than 2 points, indicate uncertainty and recommend further market research.

final.value_proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and performance of a Deere tractor with a consumer-friendly design, offering a single, integrated solution for multiple tasks.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent and refine the proposition.
final.uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated proposition is uncertain; the test will determine whether the demand is sufficient to justify investment.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent for the differentiated model is significantly lower than for a generic garden tool, we would reconsider the consumer proposition and explore alternative use cases or market segments.

frame.objective: Determine whether Deere & Company should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its tractor engineering, based on evidence available in mid-1962.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before mid-1962; no internal company data.

alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., small‑scale landscaping, hobby farming, or homeowner tasks) using tractor engineering.

position.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging John Deere’s tractor engineering. frame.objective: Determine whether Deere & Company should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its tractor engineering, based on evidence available in mid-1962.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before mid-1962; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Must identify evidence that justifies the investment, such as market demand, technical feasibility, or competitive advantage.
Consider the existing B2B2C model of independent dealer distribution and the current reach to individual buyers.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., small‑scale landscaping, hobby farming, or homeowner tasks) using tractor engineering.
2) Expand the existing B2B2C model by deepening dealer relationships and offering additional service or parts to individual buyers without a new differentiated proposition.
3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B2C model of farm and industrial equipment sold through independent dealers.
4) Target a different customer group (e.g., small‑farm owners, urban gardeners, or DIY enthusiasts) with a proposition tailored to their needs, using the same tractor platform.

X1.name: Homeowner Preference Test: Single vs Multiple Tools
X1.method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. Group A sees a description of a differentiated lawn tractor positioned as a single, integrated tool for small-scale landscaping. Group B sees the same description but positioned as a tool that reduces the number of tools needed to purchase and maintain. Both groups view a generic garden tool. Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and whether they would purchase the product.
X1.sample: 300 homeowners recruited via an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and geographic region to ensure representativeness. Randomly assigned 150 to Group A and 150 to Group B.
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and binary purchase decision (yes/no). Secondary measure: willingness to pay a premium over a generic tool.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher conversion rates than Group B, because homeowners view the tractor as a convenient, single-tool solution.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher conversion rates than Group A, because homeowners seek a single, integrated tool that reduces the number of tools they need to purchase and maintain.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 5 points higher than Group B (i.e., Group A’s average ≥ 6.5 and Group B’s average ≤ 1.5), conclude T1 is supported. If Group B’s average is at least 5 points higher, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is ≤ 1.5 points, the test is inconclusive and further data is needed.

revisions.reason: The simulated result concerns a label printer and packing errors, which does not address homeowner preferences for a differentiated lawn tractor. Therefore it does not affect T1.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging John Deere’s tractor engineering. The evidence shows a prototype was built in 1959, lawn and garden equipment sales rose 76% in 1960‑39, and the 4010 model was the most popular in the 10‑series. These points support the idea that homeowners will adopt a single, integrated tool for small tasks.
final.target_customer: Individual homeowners with small gardens who need a single tool for mowing, weeding, and light cleanup.
final.value_proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and performance of a tractor with a user‑friendly design, sold through independent dealers at a premium price.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Homeowner Preference Test (300 homeowners, 4 weeks, €2,000) to measure purchase intent and conversion rates for a differentiated lawn tractor versus a generic garden tool.
final.uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay a premium and the size of the small‑scale landscaping market are uncertain. The test will clarify whether homeowners view the tractor as a convenient, single-tool solution.
would_change_if: If the test shows a purchase intent difference of ≤ 1.5 points between the two groups, indicating no significant preference, the investment would be reconsidered.
If new evidence shows strong demand for a single, integrated tool among homeowners who already own multiple garden tools, T2 would become more likely.

position.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single-tool lawn tractor. frame.objective: Determine whether Deere & Company should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its tractor engineering, based on evidence available in mid-1962.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before mid-1962; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Must identify evidence that justifies the investment, such as market demand, technical feasibility, or competitive advantage.
Consider the existing B2B2C model of independent dealer distribution and the current reach to individual buyers.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., small‑scale landscaping, hobby farming, or homeowner tasks) using tractor engineering.
2) Expand the existing B2B2C model by deepening dealer relationships and offering additional service or parts to individual buyers without a new differentiated proposition.
3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B2C model of farm and industrial equipment sold through independent dealers.
4) Target a different customer group (e.g., small‑farm owners, urban gardeners, or DIY enthusiasts) with a proposition tailored to their needs, using the same tractor platform.

X1.name: Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition emphasizing convenience, single-tool functionality, and homeowner benefits; Group B receives a small-farm-focused proposition emphasizing versatility, multiple task capability, and small-farm owner benefits. Both groups are shown a product description of a differentiated lawn tractor (e.g., Deere 4010) and asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).
X1.sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners with small gardens and 250 small-farm owners. Recruited via online panels to ensure demographic representation.
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each group.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A.

X1.decision_rule: If the difference in average purchase intent scores between Group A and Group B is at least 1.5 points (e.g., Group A average ≥ 5.5 and Group B average ≤ 4.0), conclude the differentiated proposition aligns with the respective theory and justify investment. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, indicate uncertainty and recommend further market research.

revisions.reason: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and does not address consumer demand, homeowner behavior, or small-farm owner preferences. Therefore it does not affect the validity of T1.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single-tool lawn tractor. This aligns with the 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the established B2B2C model of independent dealer distribution.
final.target_customer: Homeowners with small gardens who need a single, convenient tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.
final.value_proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and performance of a Deere tractor with a user-friendly design, offering a single tool for multiple tasks and reducing the need for multiple equipment purchases.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent differences and determine whether to proceed with product development.
final.uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated proposition is uncertain. The test will clarify whether purchase intent is driven by consumer convenience or small-farm versatility.
would_change_if: If the test shows a difference in purchase intent of less than 1.5 points between the consumer and small-farm messages, indicating insufficient evidence to justify investment.
If new evidence shows strong demand for small-farm owners specifically, shifting the recommendation toward a small-farm proposition.

arguments.name: Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition emphasizing convenience, single-tool functionality, and homeowner benefits; Group B receives a small-farm-focused proposition emphasizing versatility, multiple task capability, and small-farm owner benefits. Both groups are shown a product description of a differentiated lawn tractor (e.g., Deere 4010) and asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).
arguments.sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners with small gardens and 250 small-farm owners. Recruited via online panels to ensure demographic representation.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each group.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A.

arguments.decision_rule: If the difference in average purchase intent scores between Group A and Group B is at least 1.5 points (e.g., Group A average ≥ 5.5 and Group B average ≤ 4.0), conclude the differentiated proposition aligns with the respective theory and justify investment. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, indicate uncertainty and recommend further market research.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

The evidence shows a 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the 4010's popularity, but it does not confirm homeowner demand for a chore-focused proposition. frame.objective: Determine whether Deere & Company should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its tractor engineering, based on evidence available in mid-1962.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before mid-1962; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Must identify evidence that justifies the investment, such as market demand, technical feasibility, or competitive advantage.
Consider the existing B2B2C model of independent dealer distribution and the current reach to individual buyers.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., small‑scale landscaping, hobby farming, or homeowner tasks) using tractor engineering.
2) Expand the existing B2B2C model by deepening dealer relationships and offering additional service or parts to individual buyers without a new differentiated proposition.
3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B2C model of farm and industrial equipment sold through independent dealers.
4) Target a different customer group (e.g., small‑farm owners, urban gardeners, or DIY enthusiasts) with a proposition tailored to their needs, using the same tractor platform.

T1.claim: Homeowners will purchase a differentiated consumer lawn tractor because it becomes an affordable, convenient chore solution for small gardens and outdoor tasks, and Deere can capture value through premium pricing and brand differentiation.
T1.who_benefits: Individual homeowners with small gardens who previously lacked efficient outdoor equipment.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Increased awareness of the convenience and practicality of garden tractors, combined with the desire for easier outdoor maintenance, makes ownership seem like a sensible purchase.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Deere can charge a premium price for a purpose-built consumer model, sell through independent dealers, and maintain brand prestige while capturing higher margins than standard farm equipment.
assumptions: Homeowners perceive garden tractors as a legitimate chore tool rather than a farm necessity.
Independent dealers will stock and service the consumer model effectively.
Marketing can communicate the value proposition to potential buyers.
predictions: A survey of homeowners will show a higher intent to purchase a consumer lawn tractor than a generic farm tractor.
Sales of the intended consumer model will exceed the sales of a comparable generic model in the same market.
